origins: In many families, money was never discussed, or it was discussed only in anger. Phrases like “Don’t ask what people earn” or “That is none of your business” can grow into the belief that any talk about money is improper. For some, church or culture added the idea that money is spiritually unclean. The result is people who cannot ask questions, plan with a spouse, or seek help.
teaches: Scripture speaks about money openly. Jesus talked about it often, and Proverbs urges us to know the state of our flocks and pay close attention to our herds. Jesus said that anyone who wants to build a tower should first sit down and count the cost. Proverbs says that the wise listen to counsel. Honest conversation about money is not shameful; it is part of stewardship, love, and wisdom, and the psalmist says that those who look to the Lord are radiant with joy and their faces will never be ashamed.
self_statements: Money is not something decent people talk about.
If I bring it up, I will look greedy.
My spouse and I should not argue about money, so we do not talk.
It is not spiritual to care about money.
errors: Believing I should never discuss money.
Feeling uncomfortable and concluding that it is wrong.
Staying away from the topic so I do not have to feel the discomfort.
Assuming others would think badly of me for asking.
questions: What did I learn about discussing money growing up?
What has my silence cost me or my family?
What would it look like to talk about money kindly and clearly?
What does Jesus say about counting the cost?
Who could I practice with first?
What question about money have I been afraid to ask?
truth: Talking about money honestly is a form of wisdom and love. I can learn to speak clearly and kindly, ask questions, and plan together with others. Shame is not required, and God’s people are not covered with shame.
hw_truths: Talking about money is part of wise stewardship.
Silence is not the same as peace.
I can speak about money kindly and clearly.
I do not have to feel shame to be careful.
log: Each week, note one conversation about money, with whom, and how it went.
actions: What do you most want to understand about your finances?
If you have a spouse or family member, set a time with no distractions and an agreed ending time.
Practice a sentence such as, “I would like us to look at our budget together so we can plan.”
If needed, meet with a nonprofit counselor or advisor and bring your questions.
prayer: Lord, You are not ashamed of me, and You care about every part of my life, including money. Free me from shame about this subject. Give me words to speak kindly and clearly, and wisdom to plan well. Amen.
hw_questions: What did I learn about money talk growing up?
What question have I been afraid to ask?
Who could I talk with first?
What would a calm money conversation sound like?
What does Jesus say about counting the cost?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Counting the cost is wise, so I can talk about money without shame.”
